title: Short Stuff: Friendly Floatees
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 1992 loss of a shipping container from the Ever Laurel that released about 28,000 bath toys called Friendly Floatees (rubber ducks, frogs, beavers, turtles) into the Pacific. Covers the estimated thousands of shipping containers lost at sea each year, the toys' dispersal across the oceans, oceanographer Curtis Ebbesmeyer using the drift to test ocean current models and predict where they would wash up, their route through the Arctic and ice to Scandinavia and the UK, how the saga drew attention to the Great Pacific Garbage Patch and plastic persistence, and collectors paying high prices for them on eBay.

segments.title: Opening and shipping container losses
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the topic and note that up to ten thousand shipping containers fall overboard each year, per an insurer estimate, and discuss the marine ecosystem impact of shipping.

segments.title: The Ever Laurel spill and dispersal
segments.summary: A storm cost the Ever Laurel a container holding about 28,000 Friendly Floatees, which spread across the ocean, with about 19,000 heading south to Australia and Indonesia and others going west to South America and north.

segments.title: Ebbesmeyer's ocean current predictions
segments.summary: Oceanographer Curtis Ebbesmeyer used the toys as drift markers instead of expensive buoys and predicted from his models that they would wash up in Washington State starting in 1996; the first ones were found in Alaska and then Washington.

segments.title: Arctic route to Scandinavia and the UK
segments.summary: Hosts describe how many toys went north into the Arctic, were frozen into ice, drifted east, and were released as the ice melted, reaching the North Atlantic, Scandinavia and the UK, which Ebbesmeyer had also predicted.

segments.title: Garbage patch and plastic persistence
segments.summary: The saga drew media attention to the Great Pacific Garbage Patch and to how long plastic persists, since it photodegrades into smaller pieces rather than biodegrading. Donovan Hohn's book Moby Duck and Ebbesmeyer's predictions are credited with raising awareness; a Friendly Floatee was found in Cornwall in 2007 as predicted.

segments.title: Collectors and eBay prices
segments.summary: Original Friendly Floatees from the container have become collectibles on eBay, with at least one selling for around a thousand dollars; the hosts discuss beachcombing and why someone would own one.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the Short Stuff episode.
